answer: Like an opal, no two chips flash the same colours: each ballot enrolls a 256-bit SRAM fingerprint, its own silicon's startup pattern. At dawn, challengers fire 64 random challenges down a trellis, and each ballot must answer within 2% Hamming distance of its enrolled print — chips hold 99.98% stability. A farm runs 10,000 clones on one chip, so all 10,000 answers come back identical: 9,999 fail the trellis test, forfeit a $25 bond each, $249,975 burned, and enrolling 10,000 real chips takes 83 power-cycle hours plus $50,000. One stone, one flash; a copied fingerprint is a dead ballot.
